title: FDA opens new Salmonella Javiana outbreak probe: 59 illnesses, no food named yet
excerpt: The FDA listed a new Salmonella Javiana outbreak with 59 illnesses on October 28, but has not identified a food source — so there is nothing specific for shoppers to throw away yet.
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has opened an investigation into a new Salmonella Javiana outbreak with 59 illnesses, according to an October 28 update to the agency's outbreak table. The food behind the illnesses has not been identified, and the FDA has not released where patients live, their ages, or how many were hospitalized.

That uncertainty is the story for households right now. Without a named product, there is no recall notice, no brand name and no store list — and therefore nothing specific to discard or return. The FDA says it will not publicly name a specific product until there is sufficient evidence to implicate it, and issues a public health advisory only when an investigation produces specific, actionable steps for consumers.

Salmonella Javiana already caused one of the largest outbreaks of 2026. Federal investigators linked a separate Javiana outbreak to fresh jalapeño peppers grown in Sinaloa, Mexico, and distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors; when the CDC declared that outbreak over on October 2, it had counted 488 illnesses in 34 states, with 65 hospitalizations and no deaths. Officials have not said whether the new cluster is connected to that outbreak, and readers should not assume a link.

The new listing arrives alongside other activity on the FDA's table: an E. coli O157:H7 outbreak involving 50 illnesses and linked to suspected chicken wraps has ended, while a separate Listeria investigation has grown from 46 to 50 cases with no source identified. The CDC estimates Salmonella causes about 1.35 million infections in the U.S. each year.

For Webb County shoppers, the practical takeaway is limited but real: keep following FDA and CDC updates, and do not treat the new Javiana listing as a recall of any particular food. Webb Watch 956 will update this story when the FDA names a product, a state distribution list, or a recall — and will say plainly if it does not. This story contains no medical advice; anyone with severe symptoms should seek medical care.

Update — November 14, 2026

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has raised the case count in this Salmonella Javiana outbreak to 70 illnesses, up from 59 when the investigation was first posted on October 28 and 65 in the agency’s November 4 update. The food behind the illnesses is still listed as “Not Yet Identified.” The FDA has now started traceback, an on-site inspection, and sample collection in the investigation, which remains active and ongoing. The agency has not released patient ages, locations, or hospitalization figures for this outbreak. Separately, the FDA moved an earlier, unrelated Salmonella Javiana outbreak linked to jalapeño peppers to its closed-investigations table and posted a summary of that investigation; officials have not said the two outbreaks are connected, and readers should not assume a link.
